visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A close-up shot captures a person's hand peeling a Pokémon card back from a large display wall in a subway station. The woman then appears with a shocked and joyful expression, holding a small packaged sticker. The background consists of a long corridor with walls covered in thousands of organized Pokémon cards. (2) The woman walks through the Zhongshan Metro Station with three children: two boys in Pikachu pajamas and a toddler girl. They approach a massive mural wall where cards can be removed. The lighting is bright and industrial, characteristic of a clean public transport hub. (3) The group stands outside the station exit, posing in front of the 'Zhongshan' sign. The woman holds the toddler while the boys make victory signs. The architecture is modern concrete with a high-contrast shadow. (4) Back inside, the children excitedly run towards the card walls. Close-up sequences show them carefully peeling stickers off the wall, revealing various Pokémon character designs. A staff member in a high-visibility green vest is seen in the background monitoring the event. (5) The woman presents three different foil-packed stickers—Pikachu, Gardevoir, and Lucario—to the camera lens. The camera pans across the wall to show the sheer scale of the interactive advertisement, with thousands of cards still attached. (6) The woman points at a large blue promotional poster for the 'Mega Evolution' series. A young boy holding a Lucario plush toy mimics the fierce pose of the character on the poster, shouting with excitement. (7) The final segment shows the woman and children descending on an escalator, holding their collected stickers. Large text overlays provide release dates and store information against the station's dark gray walls.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio opens with a driving, high-tempo electronic beat combined with a clear, resonant male narration. A sharp, high-frequency 'pop' or 'plastic peel' sound effect occurs as the first card is taken, followed immediately by the woman's high-pitched exclamation of surprise. (2) As the scene transitions to the station walk, the BGM maintains a steady, bright energy. The woman's voice exhibits high arousal and positive valence while speaking to the children, whose distant laughter creates a soft background texture. (3) A distinct 'ding' synthesizer sound effect marks the appearance of a text overlay. The male narrator's speech rate increases slightly while detailing the event specifics, his tone remaining professional and upbeat. (4) Recurrent short, percussive sound effects occur in sequence, mimicking the physical act of peeling stickers. A child's voice clearly articulates 'Pikachu' with a rising, curious intonation, which is followed by a brief 'shimmer' SFX. (5) The music swells during the promotional poster segment. A young boy provides a sudden, loud vocal outburst (simulated battle cry) that has high spectral tension and volume intensity, perfectly synchronized with a fast visual zoom. (6) The narrator delivers a final call to action with an authoritative yet friendly tone. The track concludes with a rapid-fire sequence of impact SFX for on-screen dates, ending with a clean fade-out of the electronic beat.
